# Introduction

`VariantAnnotation::readVcf()` reads VCF records and makes their
INFO and FORMAT fields available. methylVCF interprets the caller-specific
5mC fields to place each measurement at its genomic anchor. It uses DRAGEN
masks and genotypes to identify measured positions and allele or haplotype
slots, and Rastair flags to distinguish reference and de novo CpG contexts.
For a DRAGEN reference block, a measured base can be inside the block rather
than at its VCF `POS`. The resulting `GRanges` can be joined to annotations,
and reference measurements can be aligned in a `RangedSummarizedExperiment`.
[VariantAnnotation user guide][variantannotation]

Suppose you have two samples in a methylation-aware gVCF and want to compare
5mC in a short region. Start by inspecting the coverage at each site. Then
align sites across the samples. We use an artificial DRAGEN example from
the package. The workflow uses [plyranges][plyranges] to manipulate
genomic ranges and [tidySummarizedExperiment][tidyse] to work with
one row per site and sample.

# Installation

For the development version, follow the [installation instructions][install].
Once methylVCF is available on Bioconductor, install it with its tutorial
dependencies.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
BiocManager::install("methylVCF", dependencies = TRUE)
```

# Find measurements in the interval

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(methylVCF)
library(tidySummarizedExperiment)
```

```{r read}
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "dragen-multisample.g.vcf", package = "methylVCF")
region <-
    tibble::tibble(seqnames = "chr21", start = 13204474L, end = 13204520L) |>
    plyranges::as_granges()

calls <- readMethylVcf(vcf, region)
calls |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(start, sample, scope, fraction, informative_depth)
```

Each row is one reported measurement at a genomic anchor. A site can
have several rows, for example one per sample or phased allele. At
13,204,520, each sample has two phased measurements. Leave those rows in
the `GRanges` when inspecting allele-specific methylation.

The coordinates in `region` are 1-based and inclusive. To check where a
measurement came from in the gVCF, inspect `record_start` and `record_end`.
The query window starts at 13,204,474, inside the reference block that starts
at 13,204,471.

# Add a feature annotation

Add the name of a small artificial feature using an overlap join.
`join_overlap_inner()` retains the matching measurements as `GRanges`
and adds metadata from the annotation. This example joins one feature
to two measurements at its CpG.

```{r overlap}
features <-
    tibble::tibble(
        seqnames = "chr21",
        start = 13204473L,
        end = 13204476L,
        feature = "example feature"
    ) |> plyranges::as_granges()

annotated <-
    calls |>
    plyranges::join_overlap_inner(features)

annotated |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(start, feature, sample, coverage_status)
```

To retain overlapping calls without copying annotation columns, use
`plyranges::filter_by_overlaps()`.

```{r observed-overlaps}
covered <-
    calls |>
    plyranges::filter_by_overlaps(features) |>
    dplyr::filter(coverage_status == "observed")

covered |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(start, sample, fraction, informative_depth)
```

# Compare reference sites

Use `asMethylExperiment()` when the desired unit is a **reference site
by sample**. Build the experiment from the original calls so that
zero-depth reports stay available in the reported assays. The two pooled
reference sites in the example form a `RangedSummarizedExperiment` with
genomic rows and sample columns.

```{r align}
experiment <- calls |> asMethylExperiment()
```

With tidySummarizedExperiment loaded, `as_tibble()` provides a tidy view
of the assays and metadata. Keep the observed fraction and the original
report side by side to interpret the missing values.

```{r site-by-sample, warning=FALSE}
experiment |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(start, .sample, fraction, reported_fraction, informative_depth) |>
    dplyr::arrange(start, .sample)
```

At 13,204,474, the reported zero for `sample_b` has zero depth. At
13,204,515, `sample_b` has no measurement. Both analytical fractions are
missing. The recorded depth distinguishes them. The zero at 13,204,515
in `sample_a` is an observed fraction supported by nine reads.

The same projection can take a named list of imports when each file
contains a different sample. Select one VCF sample in each import, and
use a common caller format and reference assembly. The list names
become the output sample names. The importer keeps declared assemblies in
`seqinfo(calls)`. Confirm the reference assembly for files that omit it.
See the [input guide](input-vcf.html) for reader settings and format details.
